name: Monarch_get_entity
description: Get detailed information about any biomedical entity in the Monarch Initiative knowledge graph by its CURIE identifier. Supports genes (HGNC), diseases (MONDO, OMIM), phenotypes (HP), variants, and more. Returns the entity name, category, description, synonyms, cross-references, and species. Example: HGNC:11998 returns TP53 gene; MONDO:0007739 returns Huntington disease with cross-refs to OMIM, DOID, ICD10.

id.description: Entity CURIE identifier. Examples: 'HGNC:11998' (TP53), 'MONDO:0007739' (Huntington disease), 'MONDO:0005148' (type 2 diabetes), 'HP:0001250' (seizure).

deprecated.description: True if this ontology term is obsolete. Obsolete terms remain queryable but carry no annotations.

association_counts.description: How many associations the entity has in each category, each {label, category, count}, 13 entries e.g. {'label': 'Gene to Phenotype', 'category': 'biolink:GeneToPhenotypicFeatureAssociation', ...}. Read this before paging associations, to know what is there.

causes_disease.description: Diseases this entity causes, each {id, name, category}, e.g. {'id': 'MONDO:0016419', 'name': 'hereditary breast carcinoma'} -- 7 entries for TP53.

has_phenotype.description: HPO ids of the phenotypes associated with the entity, e.g. 'HP:0006572' (41 entries for TP53). Positionally parallel to has_phenotype_label.

has_phenotype_label.description: The same phenotypes by name, e.g. 'Pure red cell aplasia'. Parallel to has_phenotype -- zip the two; neither is ordered by relevance.

node_relationships.description: Typed relationships from this node, each {relation, relation_label, ...}, e.g. {'relation': 'RO:0004003', 'relation_label': 'has material basis in germline mutation in'}. The relation is what makes a gene-disease pair mean something specific.

name: Monarch_get_associations
description: Query disease-gene-phenotype associations in Monarch with exact offset pagination. Provide a subject or object CURIE; metadata reports total_results, has_more and next_offset.

object.description: Object entity CURIE. Use instead of subject to find entities associated TO this object.

category.description: Optional Biolink association category filter. Options: 'biolink:GeneToPhenotypicFeatureAssociation', 'biolink:DiseaseToPhenotypicFeatureAssociation', 'biolink:CorrelatedGeneToDiseaseAssociation', 'biolink:CausalGeneToDiseaseAssociation', 'biolink:GeneToPathwayAssociation'.

agent_type.description: Who or what produced the claim, e.g. 'manual_agent' (a human curator) versus an automated or text-mining agent.

aggregator_knowledge_source.description: Infores ids of the aggregators the claim passed through, e.g. ['infores:monarchinitiative']. The primary source is in primary_knowledge_source; this is the chain after it.

association_id.description: Monarch's id for this association, e.g. 'uuid:a769ddb6-bed6-11f1-9774-6045bd00b3c3'. A fresh UUID per build, so do not store it as a stable key.

evidence_count.description: How many pieces of evidence Monarch holds for the association, e.g. 0. Zero is common and does NOT mean the assertion is unsupported -- a manually curated assertion often carries no separate evidence rows.

knowledge_level.description: Biolink knowledge level, e.g. 'knowledge_assertion' -- a curated claim -- as opposed to 'prediction' or 'statistical_association'. The single best field for deciding how much weight an association deserves.

object_category.description: Biolink category of the object, e.g. 'biolink:Disease'.

original_object.description: The object id as the source recorded it, e.g. 'Orphanet:251579'. Monarch's `object` is usually the MONDO equivalent, so this is the only trace of which source vocabulary the claim was actually made in.

original_subject.description: The subject id as the SOURCE recorded it, before Monarch normalised it, e.g. 'NCBIGene:7157'. Compare with `subject` to see what the normalisation changed.

subject_category.description: Biolink category of the subject, e.g. 'biolink:Gene'.

subject_taxon.description: Taxon of the subject, e.g. 'NCBITaxon:9606'. A non-human taxon means the association is a model-organism finding.

subject_taxon_label.description: The same taxon by name, e.g. 'Homo sapiens'.

name: Monarch_search
description: Search the Monarch knowledge graph for biomedical entities with exact offset pagination. Metadata reports total_results, has_more and next_offset.

query.description: Search query: gene names, disease names, phenotype terms. Examples: 'BRCA1', 'Alzheimer', 'seizure', 'insulin resistance'.

category.description: Filter by entity category. Options: 'biolink:Gene', 'biolink:Disease', 'biolink:PhenotypicFeature'. Default: all categories.

deprecated.description: True if this ontology term is obsolete. Obsolete terms remain queryable but carry no annotations.

namespace.description: Which ontology the hit belongs to, e.g. 'MONDO', 'HP', 'MP'. One search returns terms from several, and mixing a human phenotype with a mouse one is a common error.

provided_by.description: Which Monarch data source supplied the node, e.g. 'phenio_nodes'.

score.description: Relevance score, e.g. 40.130344. The order is by it.

synonyms.description: Other names for the term, e.g. ['AD', ...] - 8 on the measured hit. Explains why a term whose label does not resemble the query was returned.

xrefs.description: Equivalent identifiers in other vocabularies, e.g. ['DOID:10652', ...] - 14 on the measured hit. The join to any other resource.
